# O3 · Flash Storage {.unnumbered}

The outdoor station has no SD card (see [Storing the measurements](00-design.qmd#storing-the-measurements)): its rows and its log stay in the **flash memory** of the ESP32, the memory that also holds the firmware. This first step of the firmware of the outdoor station moves the storage there. It runs on the development board of the bench as well, and is tested there before the XIAO arrives.

> **Ready-to-use project:** The complete code of this step is available in the repository here: [`firmware/paws`](https://github.com/wg1d/personal-autonomous-weather-station/tree/main/firmware/paws)

## The flash memory and LittleFS

The flash memory of the ESP32 is divided into *partitions*: one for the firmware, a few small ones for its settings, and one for files. **LittleFS** is a file system made for this kind of memory, provided with the Arduino core of the ESP32: it offers the same files and folders as the SD card, and spreads its writes over the whole partition, so that no part of the memory wears out before the others.

| Board | Flash memory | Partition for the files |
|-------|--------------|-------------------------|
| Development board of the bench | 4 MB | about 1.5 MB |
| XIAO ESP32-S3 | 8 MB | about 4.9 MB (see [The XIAO](04-2-xiao.qmd#the-memory-of-the-xiao)) |

The first time, the partition holds no file system yet: LittleFS formats it, then mounts it. The station mounts it at the first use of a wake-up, and unmounts it before the deep sleep, as it did with the SD card.

## The files

The files are those of the SD card, with one more:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `/measurements_v1.csv` | The current file of the rows, in the [CSV format v1](../Architecture/Phase-04/00-3-data-and-upload.qmd#data-format-v1) |
| `/measurements_v1_old.csv` | The previous file of the rows |
| `/upload.idx` | The upload cursor of the rows: the position of the first row the server has not acknowledged |
| `/log.txt`, `/log.old` | The current and the previous log |
| `/log.idx` | The upload cursor of the log |

## Starting a new file

The flash memory is much smaller than an SD card: the station must never fill it. Each file has a **maximum size**, a share of the partition:

| File | Share of the partition |
|------|------------------------|
| Measurements, current file | 1/4 |
| Measurements, previous file | 1/4 |
| Log, current file | 1/8 |
| Log, previous file | 1/8 |
| **Planned in all** | **3/4** |
| Margin | 1/4 |

When the current file of the rows is larger than its quarter **and** the server has acknowledged all its rows, it becomes the **previous file**, and the next row starts a new current file. The former previous file is deleted: the server has its rows, and [backs them up](../Backend/03-1-operations.qmd) every night. A new file starts when the **file** is full, not the memory: there are never more than two files of rows, and they fit in half of the partition.

The previous file is a **copy kept in the station**: if the server lost data, the [maintenance page](../Architecture/Phase-04/05-1-maintenance-mode.qmd) still gives the rows of the previous months. With one row every 15 minutes, about 7.7 KB a day, a quarter of the partition of the bench board holds about seven weeks of rows; the partition of the XIAO is about three times larger.

When the server cannot be reached, the rows are not acknowledged: the current file does not start again, and keeps growing in the margin. No row that the server does not have is ever deleted. Only if the server stays out of reach for months does the memory end up full: new rows can then no longer be stored, and the maintenance page retrieves the data.

The log follows the same pattern with an eighth of the partition, but starts a new file as soon as it is full, sent or not: the log is a help, not data.

## The rule in the core

The decision is a pure function of the core, tested on the computer like the other [rules](../Architecture/Phase-04/01-1-interfaces-and-state-machine.qmd):

```{.cpp include="../../../firmware/paws/lib/core/Rules.cpp"}
```

`isRotationDue()` is the last function: a new file starts when the file is larger than its maximum size and the upload cursor is at its end. Three tests check that the file does not start again while it is not full, that it starts again when it is full and sent, and that it is kept while rows are not sent:

```{.cpp include="../../../firmware/paws/test/test_rules/test_rules.cpp"}
```

## The adapters

`FlashVolume.h` replaces `SdCard.h`. There is no module to power any more: it mounts LittleFS, gives the size of a file, the maximum size of each kind of file, and reads the upload cursors.

```{.cpp include="../../../firmware/paws/src/adapters/FlashVolume.h"}
```

`FlashStorage.h` replaces `SdStorage.h`, with the same functions: it appends the rows and the log, reads the rows after the cursor, and saves the cursor once the server acknowledged them. `startNewFileIfFull()`, called before each row is written, applies the rule.

```{.cpp include="../../../firmware/paws/src/adapters/FlashStorage.h"}
```

The [maintenance page](../Architecture/Phase-04/05-1-maintenance-mode.qmd) reads the same files, and gains a button, **Download the previous measurements**, grayed out as long as there is no previous file. Deleting the measurements deletes both files and the cursor.

## On the bench

Build the firmware with the periods of the bench, one row per minute and one upload every five minutes, and send it to the board:

```bash
pixi run pio run -d firmware/paws -e esp32-bench -t upload -t monitor
```

An SD card module left wired stays off: the pull-down resistor of its power pin keeps it off. On our board, a wake-up with an upload printed:

```text
PAWS firmware v0.9.0-12-g7e9d1f6-dirty (bench periods)
-> BOOT
-> MEASURE
-> STORE
   stored: 2026-10-12T14:25:00Z,1,22.47,53.60,1003.09
-> UPLOAD
   Wi-Fi connected in 200 ms
   sent 282 bytes of measurements, server answered 200 {"received":5,"inserted":5,"duplicates":0}
   sent 1371 bytes of log, server answered 200 {"received":59}
-> SCHEDULE
   alarm set for 14:26:00
-> SLEEP
   awake for 2212 ms
```

The five rows of the previous minutes are sent at once, and the server stores them all. The wake-ups without upload last less than a second. The maintenance page showed the size of the rows stored, and gave the measurements and the log to download.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---------|---------------|
| `[E][vfs_api.cpp:105] open(): /littlefs/log.idx does not exist, no permits for creation` | Printed by the Arduino core of the ESP32 when the station checks whether a file exists, and it does not yet: here, the cursor of the log before its first upload. Nothing to fix: the cursor is created right after, and the message does not come back. |
| `flash file system not mounted` | The partition for the files is missing from the partition table of the board, or the flash memory is damaged. The rows are not stored, but the station keeps its schedule. |
| `NOT stored` with a mounted file system | The memory is full: the server has not acknowledged the rows for a long time. Download them from the maintenance page, then bring the server back. |
